subject: Post-call: Fincrest evaluation convergence checklist & proposed live tests
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alejandra Molina <amolina@fincrest.com>
Cc: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@fincrest.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Fincrest evaluation convergence checklist & proposed live tests

Hi Alejandra — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed path to produce apples-to-apples results versus your incumbents.

Key pain points you called out
- Latency spikes on peak batch scoring (3k–5k requests/min) causing timeouts in the ingestion pipeline
- Unpredictable per-token cost across models with current vendor (variance by 3x depending on prompt length)
- Limited ability to run private deployments in your VPC with audit logging and customer-managed KMS

Goals you shared
- Stable p95 latency under 150ms for 512-token scoring workload
- Predictable cost per 1k queries within a 20% band versus benchmarks
- Ability to run a private deployment in GCP us-central1 with SOC2-ready audit trails

What we propose (short experiment plan)
1) Live throughput test: 10-minute 3k RPM burst using a mirror of your scoring pipeline (we provide a test harness).
2) Cost/latency sweep: run identical prompt sets across three model variants (open-llama-70b, redwood-mini-quant, and vendor-stable) to capture p50/p95, token consumption, and KV-cache hit rates.
3) VPC validation: deploy Redwood Private in a trial VPC with KMS integration and sample audit events.

Open questions we need answered to scope the test:
- Can you share a representative prompt set (redact PII) and the average token length distribution?
- Do you have a preference for GPU family for isolated tests (A100 vs H100) or should we match your current production hardware?
- Any regulatory constraints on telemetry we should exclude from outbound logs?

Attachments: I attached an evaluation checklist and an initial test plan (Redwood-Eval-Checklist-v1.xlsx / Redwood-TestPlan-v1.xlsx). Marcus will run the throughput harness and Karthik will lead the model-sweep.

Proposed next steps
- You confirm prompt set and preferred hardware by EOD Monday (11 May).
- We schedule the 10-minute burst window for Wed 13 May (you pick timezone).
- Redwood provides results + a short readout within 48 hours of test completion.

If that all sounds good I’ll create the HubSpot activities and lock the test windows.

Thanks — Laura

Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Laura — thanks for the fast recap and clear plan. This aligns well. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Prompt set: I attached a redacted sample (sent as a separate link via our SFTP). Average sequence = ~420 tokens; 90th pct = ~1,200 tokens.
2) Hardware: We currently run A100s in prod; H100 is available in our test account if you think it will change outcomes. Leaning to A100 for parity.
3) Telemetry: We cannot export raw user text off-platform; aggregated metrics and token counts are fine. Any logs leaving our VPC need to be sanitized.

Procurement note: our security team will request the standard vendor questionnaire and an initial SOC2 evidence package ahead of any private deployment. I can introduce you to our security lead, Jorge (cc’d).

One more ask: How do you plan to measure the vendor’s existing cache behavior? We need to ensure the comparison accounts for prefix caching strategies.

—Alejandra
Alejandra Molina

Thanks for the details, Alejandra — very helpful. A few technical clarifications and how we’ll handle cache parity across vendors: 

- Cache strategy: for the vendor baseline we’ll run two sweep modes: (A) cold-start (no prefix cache) and (B) warm-start with a controlled prefix cache layer that imitates your production session reuse. This will let us isolate savings from caching vs model and infra.
- Token accounting: Redwood test harness reports tokenized counts and normalizes across tokenizers to the same BPE standard so per-token cost comparison is apples-to-apples.
- Hardware: we’ll default to A100 for parity but can repeat on H100 if you want to see delta.
- Telemetry sanitization: we will run the tests in your VPC; aggregated metrics are exported. Any payloads that leave the VPC will be redacted based on a shared regex—happy to sync with your security team on the exact sanitation rules.

Marcus will own running the 10-minute 3k RPM burst (we’ll provide a replay harness that hits the same endpoints you do). Marcus, plan is to produce these outputs per run: p50/p95 latency, token throughput, KV-cache hit rate, and per-1k-query cost estimate.

Open technical questions from Redwood
- Is there a synthetic traffic generator or replay you prefer we use, or shall we mirror your ingress logs?
- For the private deployment audit trail: which KMS do you want us to integrate (GCP KMS or external HSM)?

Next steps: Laura — if you’re good, I’ll draft a short test-run checklist and timeline and post to the Drive link Laura shared.

Karthik
